context:
The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms. It was first observed by Robert Hooke in 1665. The cell theory states:
  • All living things are made of cells.
  • The cell is the basic unit of life.
  • All cells arise from pre-existing cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered the 'structural and functional unit' of all living organisms?
questions.reason: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of the body, and all living beings are made up of cells.

questions.question: The cell wall in plant cells is primarily composed of ______.
questions.reason: The cell wall is a non-living rigid layer in plant cells mainly composed of cellulose.

questions.question: Mitochondria
questions.reason: Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell, producing ATP through cellular respiration.

questions.question: Ribosomes
questions.reason: Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis in the cell.

questions.question: Chloroplast
questions.reason: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis in plant cells.

question: Which cell organelle is known as the 'suicide bag' of the cell?
reason: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that destroy organelles when the cell is old or injured, earning them the name 'suicide bags'.

question: Arrange the following stages of cell division in the correct sequence.
reason: Mitosis proceeds in the order Prophase → Metaphase → Anaphase → Telophase (PMAT).

question: Describe the role of the nucleus in a cell.
answer:
The nucleus is the control centre of the cell. It contains DNA (genetic material) that directs all cellular activities, including:
  • Growth
  • Metabolism
  • Reproduction
reason: The nucleus regulates gene expression and manages cell division through the DNA it contains.

question: Explain the difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
answer: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles (e.g., bacteria). Eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles (e.g., plant and animal cells).
reason: The key distinction is the presence or absence of a membrane-bound nucleus.

question: The ______ is known as the powerhouse of the cell.
reason: Mitochondria produce ATP through cellular respiration, supplying the cell with energy.

question: The chemical formula for glucose is C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>. During photosynthesis, CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O → C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> + O<sub>2</sub>. Which organelle performs this reaction?
reason: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis in plant cells.

question: Mitochondria are often called the powerhouse of the cell because they produce ATP through cellular respiration.
reason: Mitochondria generate ATP via cellular respiration, supplying energy for all cellular activities.
